svg.text: 12 karaoke cursors for the lyrics overlay · Glass Orb style · default coral #FF3F4C
Recolor any of them by setting color, or when inlined, color: var(--lg-bouncer). Bodies use currentColor; highlights are a white sheen plus a dark overlay.
The classic karaoke ball: a soft glowing orb that hops along the
at the top of the hop, flattens on landing,
then settles. A soft glow pulses slightly
louder at the apex. Optional contact shadow
scales out as it leaves the word.
A chunky eighth note that marks the beat as each word is sung.
Tilts back about 18° while airborne, tips
forward on landing, and lightly squashes
through the note head. The flag can give a
stem by a frame or two).
A four-point sparkle star that twinkles over the active lyric.
twinkles with a short scale pulse at the

A bold heart that sits on the sung word — clear even at tray-like
Pulses (a quick beat-scale) as it lands,
with a mild squash in the lower tip. Slight
sideways tilt in the air, then a spring
back to upright. Can double-pulse on a held
A glassy teardrop, like a bead of light resting on the lyric
Stretches into a taller drop at the apex,
then a wet squash on landing (wide and
shear) as it settles. The highlight can
slide up the left edge during the hop.
A tiny lantern bug: glowing abdomen, faint glass wings, and a
Hover more than bounce — a softer landing
with less squash, a constant idle bob, and
a glow that pulses independently of the
hop. Wings flutter with a short
scale/rotate loop. On a held note it can
A bright nucleus with a trailing tail that streams behind the
squash-and-stretch as Glow Orb. The tail
always streams opposite the hop direction:
long and loose in the air, compressed or
tucked on landing. In RTL lyrics, flip the
tail with scaleX(-1) so it still…
Three rounded equalizer bars that bounce as a little meter on the
The group hops as one, but each bar
beat. On landing the whole meter squashes
flatter. On a held note the bars can keep
A tiny handheld microphone — the karaoke object itself, hopping
while airborne, then squashes through the
capsule on landing. A very small “sound
ring” can flash around the grille at the
A folded paper dart that banks from word to word like a short
Banks (rolls) into the hop, glides with the
nose slightly up, then dips the nose and
flattens on landing. Travel between words
can include a short horizontal glide, not
only a vertical bounce. In RTL, flip with
A chunky square pixel with a 1-bit highlight — like a cursor on
Snappy, not fluid. The hop can be stepped
(a few discrete frames) rather than eased.
On landing it flattens into a wider
rectangle for one frame, then pops back.

A thick crescent moon that rocks gently over the sung word.
Rocks like a little hammock: tilts back

independent of the hop, for a quieter
